[Architecture overview](../export-design.html).

## Files and failures — What CSV conventions and output names do we use, and what happens when a trip export fails? {#files-and-failures-what-csv-conventions-and-output-names-do-we-use-and-what-happens-when-a-trip-export-fails}

Source extraction uses the default `sql/csv` format. It writes one `<qualified-table>.csv` per table.

See the [trip-loading guide](../../source-loading.html) for the encoding, headers and NULL representation.

Decide what to retain and whether to continue with other trips when one export fails.

## Export selected trips

Export one trip at a time, producing one ROS Excel workbook for that trip.

For each selected trip ID:

1. Extract its ObServe dataset, with one CSV per ObServe sheet.
2. Transform that dataset into the selected ROS form model.
3. Populate one ROS workbook for that trip.
4. Validate that workbook and retain its validation result.

A multi-trip selection produces multiple workbooks. It does not produce a combined workbook that needs splitting.

```text
Selection criteria
        ↓
List of ObServe trip IDs
        ↓ for each trip ID
ObServe CSV dataset → ROS sheet data → One ROS workbook → ROS validation
```

## Populate and validate the ROS form

Use `form.tools` to populate the matching ROS template and `ros.form.validation` to validate the resulting workbook.

Keep the generated form and its validation result associated with the selected ObServe trip.

Output naming, per-trip failure handling and batch summaries remain to be defined.
